raw_response:
I found three useful catalogue-derived components for the named-constant problem. None has verified availability before the 2007-05-18 cutoff: attrs is positively later, while the inspected Better Enums and Magic Enum pages remain date-unknown. The applications below are translations by an internal model, not evidence of deployment or demonstrated usefulness.

1. attrs frozen value classes with type-checked ordering — https://github.com/python-attrs/attrs

   Why it could help: A frozen class per constant family can provide same-type equality and opt-in ordinal comparison without inheriting ordinary integer arithmetic.
   
   Application: Give each family a separate class, store its name and ordinal, and keep the allowed instances in an immutable ordered registry. The comparison documentation checks types before comparing fields; the examples show rejection of ordinary reassignment.
   
   Constraint: This requires custom construction control, canonicalization, and registry logic. Frozen instances alone do not create a closed enumeration, and the protection is best-effort.
   
   Discovery catalogue opened: https://github.com/vinta/awesome-python
   Verifying sources opened: https://www.attrs.org/en/stable/comparison.html and https://www.attrs.org/en/stable/examples.html
   Date: post-decision. https://www.attrs.org/en/stable/changelog.html dates the initial release to 2015-04-15 and the frozen option to 2016-08-30; the inspected documentation is for 26.1.0, released 2026-03-19.

2. Better Enums declaration-generated enum tables — https://aantron.github.io/better-enums/

   Why it could help: A single enum declaration generates name lookup, validation, and declaration-order iteration, offering a concrete model for keeping the named member set consistent.
   
   Application: Transfer the generated member table and index lookup design into a Python class factory, then explicitly compare ordinals only within the same family.
   
   Constraint: This is a C++ design reference. Default integer conversion breaks the required isolation; the strict-conversion option requires C++11. Duplicate backing values also need rejection because they can make names and indices ambiguous.
   
   Discovery catalogue opened: https://github.com/fffaraz/awesome-cpp
   Verifying sources opened: https://aantron.github.io/better-enums/ApiReference.html and https://aantron.github.io/better-enums/tutorial/ScopeAndSafety.html
   Date: unknown. The documentation is version 0.11.3 with a 2015-2019 copyright footer, but no release publication date or pre-cutoff version was verified.

3. Magic Enum metadata sequences and optional operators — https://github.com/Neargye/magic_enum

   Why it could help: Separate value/name sequences and checked lookup APIs show how traversal and identification can be exposed independently of optional flag operators.
   
   Application: Use this separation as an API reference for a symbolic-value type: expose immutable member metadata and deliberate conversion operations, and add only operations meaningful to that family.
   
   Constraint: The implementation depends on modern C++ enum semantics and reflection. Numeric aliases can collapse to one reflected name, compiler-specific scans have bounds, and a Python design still needs its own order policy and closed member universe.
   
   Discovery catalogue opened: https://github.com/fffaraz/awesome-cpp
   Verifying sources opened: https://github.com/Neargye/magic_enum and https://github.com/Neargye/magic_enum/blob/master/doc/limitations.md
   Date: unknown. Only live master documentation was inspected; its modern C++ requirements do not establish a dated publication or pre-cutoff availability.

Search limitations: Restricted queries nevertheless exposed off-catalogue Python enum pages, which were excluded from discovery. One external Python-patterns page was opened prematurely and excluded together with its entries. The dylanhogg awesome-python list body could not be retrieved. These exclusions do not erase exposure, and prior model knowledge is not controlled.
